title: Inline cell editing and focus stability for virtualized tables
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Our virtualized table unmounts offscreen rows aggressively to maintain performance. When a user starts inline editing a cell, then scrolls or a re-render happens (sorting/filtering, density change, or data refresh), focus is lost, the editor unmounts, and the cursor position and edit state are often lost. This causes data loss risk and poor keyboard/assistive tech experience.

Goal: Define a UX and implementation contract that preserves edit state and keyboard focus for inline cell editors in virtualized tables while keeping memory and rendering costs bounded. Produce design specs, accessible announcements, keyboard flows, and a developer integration pattern for the DS Table component and the hosting app to follow.

Out of scope: full collaborative editing, complex cell widgets (rich text with attachments), or backend autosave protocols beyond a lightweight debounce autosave pattern.

Key outcomes:
- Users can initiate inline edit via keyboard or mouse and continue editing even if the row leaves the immediate viewport briefly (e.g., due to programmatic data updates, sorting change, density toggle).
- No perceptible regressions to virtualization memory and CPU budgets for typical large datasets (10k+ rows).
- Clear accessibility announcements and ARIA attributes so screen reader users are aware of editor entry/exit and save status.

Constraints and considerations:
- Must work with existing continuous virtualization (windowing) strategy used by the runtime team and not require rendering the entire table.
- Editors should be treated as ephemeral 'sticky' components: when editing starts, we should pin a lightweight representation to a floating layer (portal) that preserves position relative to viewport until edit completes or cancels.
- Need a stable identity/keying scheme per row and cell so focus restoration can be attempted if the original row is remounted.
- For grouped or multi-column layouts (column reorder, pinned columns), editor positioning must account for pinned regions and horizontal scroll.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Activation: editor activates in-place as today. Component emits an "editor-start" event with {rowId, columnId, cellValue, editorType}.
2) Sticky portal: upon editor-start, Table mounts a lightweight portal layer that duplicates the editor UI and pins it to the viewport coordinates of the original cell. The portal contains minimal DOM for input and controls; it consumes no table row DOM. The original cell can unmount without losing edit state.
3) Ownership & autosave: the portal owns transient edit state and exposes a small API: save(), cancel(), syncToRowWhenAvailable(). Autosave debounce default 1.5s, configurable via prop.
4) Focus behavior and restoration: keyboard focus is moved into the portal editor. If the row is remounted within a configurable time window (default 5s), component attempts to sync portal state back into the cell and transfer focus to the in-row editor and unmount portal. If not remounted, portal stays until save/cancel or explicit blur.
5) Accessibility: announce "Editing cell at column <name> row <n>" on start. On save: "Edit saved" with polite live region. Use aria-describedby linking to validation messages for editor controls. Ensure ESC cancels and returns focus to previous logical place.
6) Visual continuity: subtle elevation and border change to indicate portal mode; transition animation to reduce perceived jump when transferring back to in-row editor.
7) Developer API: Table exposes composable hooks: useTableEditorManager(rowKey) and EditorSlot component contract so apps can provide custom editors that work with the portal pattern.

Trade-offs considered:
- Portal increases complexity but keeps virtualization benefits by not forcing full row render.
- Pinning editors for long durations can increase memory; we limit portal lifetime and require apps to opt-in heavy editors.
- Sync conflicts if underlying data changed while editing: default conflict resolution is last-write-wins with an optional onConflict hook for apps to present a reconciliation UI.

Open questions for Eng:
- Can existing virtualization anchor logic expose exact viewport coordinates reliably across pinned columns?
- Are there performance regressions on low-end machines when many editors are opened? Suggested mitigations: single-portal instance per table and pooled input components.

Rollout plan:
- Design spec + interactive prototype in Figma (iteration 1) -> internal review (1 week).
- Small engineering spike (ENG spike) to validate portal approach and measure perf (2 weeks).
- Implement Table hook and example editor in DS (3 sprints).
- Ship behind feature flag with console pages using inline editing for staged validation.
- Gather telemetry: editor open time, focus-lost events, canceled edits, save errors.

Metrics for success:
- Reduce reported keyboard/focus loss incidents to near zero for inline edit flows.
- No more than 5% regression in table render/scroll FPS in benchmarks for typical workloads.
- Positive qualitative feedback from internal product teams after staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Users can start inline edit with keyboard/mouse and continue editing if the originating row unmounts due to virtualization or transient updates
Focus remains inside an active editor until the user saves or cancels; screen reader announces editor state changes
Portal editor syncs back to in-row editor when the original row remounts within configured timeframe
Developer-facing API hooks exist and are documented with an example editor implementation
Performance: no more than 5% FPS regression in standard table benchmarks with 10k rows
Edge cases: ESC restores focus predictably, blur behavior is configurable, and conflict hook triggers when underlying data changes
dev_notes: Prefer single portal container per Table instance to limit DOM churn and memory
Row and cell keys must be stable across sorts/filters; use model-ids rather than index-based keys
Portal should calculate position using getBoundingClientRect + table scroll offsets; account for pinned columns by measuring pinned container
Expose hooks for editor lifecycle: onStart, onSave, onCancel, onSyncAttempt
Conflict resolution: default last-write-wins; provide onConflict callback to UI layer

2026-03-11: Accessibility announcements will use polite ARIA live region and verbalized column name rather than numeric index to aid screen reader users

qa_notes: Test keyboard flow: Enter to edit, ESC to cancel, Tab cycles within editor fields then exits to next logical cell
Test screen reader: NVDA/VoiceOver announce editing start/finish and validation messages
Simulate rapid sort/filter changes while editing to validate state preservation and sync behavior
Open multiple editors across different rows; ensure single-portal instance behaves and doesn’t leak memory
Stress test with 10k rows and random density toggles; capture FPS and memory traces
